You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Nasdaq Closes at a Record; Meta Surges 11.34%; Bitcoin Breaks Above $86,000 (September 22, 2026)

TEXT:
Market reference: Precious metals, crude oil , the US dollar and cryptocurrencies use September 22 morning webpage quotes. Crypto data are as of approximately 09:02 Beijing time. US equities use the September 21 regular-session close.
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Officials maintain a hawkish tone as additional tightening remains under discussion
St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said further rate increases would likely be needed to contain persistent inflation and argued that gradual tightening could reduce the need for more disruptive action later.
The Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points on September 16, taking the target range to 3.75%–4.00%. Its latest projections indicate that one additional increase could still occur in 2026.
Markets remain divided over the next decision. With few major US releases scheduled for September 22, attention turns to Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin’s remarks.
Market Impact : Lower oil prices and Treasury yields have temporarily eased valuation pressure, but Fed officials have not signaled a policy pivot. Further gains in technology stocks and cryptocurrencies will partly depend on whether inflation, energy prices and long-term yields continue to moderate.
International Commodities
Oil gives back part of its risk premium as diplomacy and Saudi exports ease supply concerns
Saudi Arabia increased crude loadings through its Gulf terminals, partially offsetting disruption caused by earlier attacks on its East-West pipeline.
President Donald Trump said he would be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian during the UN General Assembly, prompting markets to reassess the probability of further supply disruption.
Brent settled near $100.34 on September 21 and traded around $100.41 on September 22 morning. WTI futures were approximately $92.32.
Market Impact : The pullback in oil reduces near-term inflation and bond-yield pressure, supporting growth stocks. Middle Eastern transport routes and energy facilities nevertheless remain exposed to security risks, leaving some geopolitical premium in crude prices.
International Macroeconomic Policy
US and China plan an AI incident channel, while the trade truce remains unresolved
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two countries agreed to establish a formal AI-safety dialogue and explore a communication mechanism for major AI incidents.
Officials plan to meet again in Shenzhen in approximately two months to discuss risks including uncontrollable agents, non-state cyber activity and developer accountability.
The current tariff truce expires on November 10, and no extension has been agreed. This week’s expected Trump–Xi meeting is likely to cover trade, AI and the Middle East.
Market Impact : A formal AI dialogue could reduce the risk of policy miscalculation, but the unresolved trade truce remains an important variable for technology, semiconductor and cross-border supply-chain companies.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot gold : Approximately $4,359.88 per ounce.
Silver futures : Approximately $67.17 per ounce.
WTI crude oil futures : Approximately $92.32 per barrel, November 2026 contract.
Brent crude oil futures : Approximately $100.41 per barrel, November 2026 contract.
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approximately 100.15.
US 10-year Treasury yield : Approximately 4.95%.
Driver Analysis : Lower crude prices and a 10-year Treasury yield below 5% eased concerns about energy-driven inflation. Gold remains supported by geopolitical risk, central-bank purchases and fiscal concerns, while a stronger dollar and expectations for further rate increases provide resistance.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approximately 86,428 USDT, up around 5.94% over 24 hours.
ETH : Approximately 2,768 USDT, up around 4.53% over 24 hours.
Total cryptocurrency market capitalization : Approximately $2.97 trillion.
Indicative 24-hour volume : Approximately $26.87 billion for BTC and $11.95 billion for ETH.
Price, Volume and Large-Buyer Activity : Both assets advanced sharply, with Bitcoin holding above $86,000. Strategy disclosed that it purchased 950 BTC for approximately $75.7 million between September 14 and 20 at an average price of about $79,670. BitMine acquired 27,562 ETH during the week through September 20, taking its holdings to 5,983,940 ETH. These are newly disclosed weekly purchases, not intraday purchases made on September 22.
Driver Analysis : Spot ETF inflows, short covering, improving US regulatory sentiment and stronger risk appetite supported the rally. Continued corporate accumulation provides structural demand, although leverage and profit-taking risks have increased following the sharp advance.
US Equity Index Performance
